subject: Reserved GPU Commitment — pricing floor contingency & approval matrix
messages:
From: Sarah Cho <procurement@aureliahealth.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFQ follow-up — committed capacity and pricing flexibility

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Aurelia is excited about Redwood's predictable latency profile for our patient-facing summarization workloads. Procurement asked me to capture a couple of specifics so we can include them in the SOW and share with our finance committee:

- Minimum committed GPU hours / month you recommend for our expected peak Q4 load (we estimated ~45M tokens/day).
- Options for a 12 vs 24 month reserved commitment (pricing delta and any trigger/escape clauses).
- Clarity on how GPU price inflation would be handled (indexation, pass-through, or discount ladder).

We received an internal ask to surface any fallback/upgrade rules (e.g., if we need burst capacity beyond reserved pool) and whether a discount floor can be offerable in the event of a sustained GPU price spike.

I attached the draft SOW (Aurelia_SOW_v3.pdf) — we've redlined a few service-level expectations. Can you send a proposal by end of next week so we can circulate?

Best,
Sarah Cho
Senior Procurement Manager
Aurelia Health

Attachments: Aurelia_SOW_v3.pdf (PDF, 142KB)
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Cho <procurement@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 14:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFQ follow-up — committed capacity and pricing flexibility

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the SOW and the clear asks. Quick responses up front:

- For your Q4 peak (45M tokens/day) our sizing heuristic suggests ~180–220 reserved A100-equivalent GPU hours/day for latency-sensitive inference (continuous load profile assumed). That maps to a monthly commit in the 5.4k–6.6k GPU-hour range.
- 12 vs 24 month: typical delta is 8–14% effective unit discount for 24mo vs 12mo depending on SKU mix and burst profile.
- GPU price shock: we can offer a guarded discount floor plus a price-band trigger. We typically structure this as: a baseline unit price locked to the quarter signed, a reconciliation band (±X% market movement) with a capped pass-through, and an executive-level safety net for >Y% market movement.

I'm looping in Marissa for commercial guidance and Karthik/Kim from finance for the specific approval matrix and any price-contingency constraints. Will attach our sensitivity model (gpu-cost-sensitivity-model.xlsx) for transparency.

Would it help if we propose two alternative term structures: (A) 12mo with conservative burst credits and a tighter discount; (B) 24mo with deeper discount and a predefined indexation ladder? If so I'll send a formal term sheet next iteration.

Thanks — talk soon.

—Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
nikhil@redwoodinference.com
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Aurelia Health — sizing + pricing sensitivity ask (need approval guidance)

Team —

Aurelia (prospect, HEALTH-tech) is asking for committed capacity options and explicit language for GPU price shocks. They estimated ~45M tokens/day for Q4. Initial sizing from infra is ~180–220 A100-equivalent GPU-hours/day (5.4k–6.6k GPU-hours/month).

I ran the sensitivity model and attached it (gpu-cost-sensitivity-model.xlsx). Key outputs:
- At current market cost (baseline), 24mo yields ~12% lower unit price than 12mo.
- If GPU spot-equivalent costs rise by 30% sustained over a quarter, our margin compresses ~8–10% under a fixed-price 24mo without an indexation clause.

Customer requests: a discount floor (protect them from upside) + a trigger that re-opens pricing if vendor GPU costs increase beyond a threshold. They also want burst capacity SLAs and defined failover to hosted model variants.

Asks:
1) What is the max commercial discount we can commit to for a 24mo deal at this size without Exec approval?
2) Would finance accept a capped pass-through (e.g., pass-through only after >20% market movement, capped at +12% unit price) vs a rebate escrow?
3) Any mandatory language we should avoid on indexation that will create accounting complications?

I've populated the file with scenario tabs (low/med/high GPU inflation) and an approval ladder recommendation. If helpful, Ethan Morales from CloudVendor (their ops contact) copied below can confirm our vendor SKU mapping.

Thanks — Nikhil

Attachments: gpu-cost-sensitivity-model.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aurelia Health — sizing + pricing sensitivity ask (need approval guidance)

Thanks for the model, Nikhil — good work on the scenario breakdown. My quick take:

- For a deal of this scale and strategic value we can stretch commercial levers, but we need to cap downside to the company. I recommend the following commercial guardrails:
  * 24mo target: up to 14% unit discount vs retail list, conditional on a minimum 85% utilization of committed pool in months 7–12.
  * 12mo target: up to 8% unit discount with standard burst credits (30% of committed capacity/month at reduced discount).
  * Burst SLA: guaranteed access to additional hosted burst pool with 48–72 hour provisioning SLA (operationally practical).

- GPU price shock construct: prefer capped pass-through after a 20% sustained vendor cost movement over a 60-day rolling window. Pass-through capped at +12% unit price. Below that threshold we absorb volatility. For any pass-through >12% we escalate to Exec for a discretionary credit to customer.

- Approval matrix: discounts up to 10% can be approved by Sales Director (Marissa). 10–14% requires VP Sales + Finance (Kimberly). >14% requires CFO/CEO review.

Kimberly / Karthik — please confirm finance comfort with the 20% trigger and 12% cap. If you need alternative language (escrow, rebate), flag now.

Marissa
VP, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 16:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aurelia Health — sizing + pricing sensitivity ask (need approval guidance)

Confirming finance position after reviewing the sensitivity workbook. Short answer: acceptable with conditions.

- We sign off on the 20% sustained cost movement trigger with a 60-day rolling window and a pass-through cap at +12% unit price. The cap preserves margin headroom and is administratively straightforward.
- For the 24mo at proposed scale (5.4k–6.6k GPU-hours/month), we approve up to 14% unit discount provided the utilization covenant is included (85% in months 7–12) and a quarterly utilization report is delivered.
- If the pass-through is invoked >6% in a quarter, we require a quarterly exception review and the option to apply a one-time credit (up to 1.5% ARR-equivalent) to smooth customer impact — this lives in a deferred credit liability.

Operational asks (to include in SOW):
- Clear SKU mapping (A100-equivalent vs on-demand variants) and guidance on fallback model latency/quality.
- Reporting cadence and template for utilization + cost-reconciliation.
- Burstable pool definition and invoice treatment for burst usage.

Nikhil — you have finance approval to present the two-term structure to Aurelia with the clauses above. Anything beyond 14% discount or more aggressive pass-through will need CFO sightline (loop in me and the revenue operations lead).

Kimberly Park
Director, Finance — Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposal: Commitment terms & GPU-price contingency (Aurelia Health)

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the patience — attaching a concise proposal reflecting our internal approvals. High level: two options to choose from.

Option A — 12 months (conservative)
- Commit: 5.4k GPU-hours/month
- Discount: 8% off list
- Burst credits: up to 30% of committed pool/month with 48–72h provisioning SLA
- Price-shock: Redwood absorbs <20% vendor cost movement. After a sustained 20% move (60-day rolling), pass-through up to +12% unit price.

Option B — 24 months (preferred for unit economics)
- Commit: 6.2k GPU-hours/month (phased ramp over first two quarters)
- Discount: 12% off list (up to 14% conditional on utilization covenant)
- Utilization covenant: 85% of committed pool in months 7–12; quarterly reporting required
- Price-shock: same 20% trigger and +12% cap; any pass-through >6% triggers a quarterly exception review and potential smoothing credit.

Operational items we will include in the draft SOW: SKU mapping, fallback model variants for latency/quality tradeoffs, reporting template, and billing treatment for bursts.

Please let us know which option you prefer and we will circulate a redlined term sheet. Happy to set a call next week to walk the Aurelia finance committee through the sensitivity model.

Best regards,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
nikhil@redwoodinference.com
